review_output: {"summary":"Prior MAJOR is fixed: the admission FOR UPDATE lock serializes count+insert, and an existing-requestId retry bypasses quota without inserting. No new critical or major issues in the supplied source. Three minor items remain: 429 Retry-After also sent for permanent total-limit exhaustion, FOR UPDATE stronger than needed (blocks FK child inserts), and quota bound only per admission. Pending content-validation integration not reviewed or accepted.","findings":[{"file":"src/app/api/live-metrics/[vendorId]/[liveId]/sessions/route.ts","area":"quota/HTTP semantics","severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.8,"issue":"MetricSessionLimitError doesn't say whether the open or total limit was hit, so 429 Retry-After:30 is also sent when 64 total sessions are used up, which is permanent for that admission.","evidence":"A single MetricSessionLimitError covers both the usage.open and usage.total checks. The route always returns Retry-After \"30\".","impact":"Clients keep retrying forever after the total limit is exhausted. This wastes rate-limit budget and suggests a recovery that can never happen.","recommended_fix":"Add a reason to the error (open vs total). Send 429 with Retry-After only for open. For total, return a terminal response (e.g. 409 or 429) without Retry-After and require a new admission.","required_test":"After 64 closed sessions, an N+1 request returns a terminal response without Retry-After. When 16 sessions are open, it still returns 429 with Retry-After."},{"file":"src/lib/live-metric-session.ts","area":"locking/availability","severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.65,"issue":"The admission lock uses FOR UPDATE, which conflicts with FOR KEY SHARE. While this transaction runs (up to 10s), other transactions' FK inserts and key-share locks on that LiveViewerSession are blocked.","evidence":"SELECT id FROM \"LiveViewerSession\" ... FOR UPDATE is held through the resolver, re-resolve, revalidate and insert. Only issuance-vs-issuance serialization is needed.","impact":"Needless contention or stalls for interval ingestion, chat, or heartbeat writes that reference the admission. Deadlocks surface as 503s.","recommended_fix":"Use FOR NO KEY UPDATE. It still serializes issuances (they conflict with each other) without blocking FK FOR KEY SHARE checks.","required_test":"While an issuance holds the admission lock, a concurrent FK child insert referencing that admission proceeds. Two concurrent issuances stay serialized, and the N+1 quota test still passes."},{"file":"src/lib/live-metric-session.ts","area":"quota scope/binding","severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.5,"issue":"The quota counts only by admission, and the sources SQL never binds the admission to the submission. Sessions per registration are therefore limited only by how many admissions a viewer can get.","evidence":"The usage query filters by admissionSessionId/vendorId/liveId. The sources query joins admission only on liveId/vendorId. Any binding relies on resolveVerifiedPrivateChatViewer, whose code wasn't supplied.","impact":"If admissions can be reissued (e.g. on rejoin), one verified registration can create sessions without limit.","recommended_fix":"Enforce admission↔submission binding in SQL if the schema has it. Also add a per-registration total cap counted under the registration or submission lock.","required_test":"One submission with several fresh admissions gets rejected once the per-registration cap is reached. An admission token paired with another viewer's chat session gets 403."}]}
